blocks.t: Welcome to Orient's Hotpot Chronicles, a Fabric mod that brings sharing a hotpot meal into Minecraft. Build a stove, set a copper or iron pot on top, pour in broth, add tripe and fatty beef rolls, then pick up a bite with chopsticks, dip it in your own sauce, and enjoy.
This guide has two parts: learning to play and looking things up.

entries.title: Your First Hotpot in Ten Minutes

blocks.t: Follow these six steps from scratch to your first bite of hotpot. Each step includes its recipe.
Step 1: Craft a stove
Place the stove on the ground. Right-click its brick body with an empty hand to open the firebox screen.
Put fuel in the fuel slot. Anything a vanilla furnace burns works: planks, logs, charcoal, coal, lava buckets, and more. Stronger heat cooks faster (see Stoves & Hotpots).
Step 2: Craft a pot and set it on the stove
Iron and copper pots work the same; only their appearance differs. Hold the pot and right-click the stove to place it. Its two handles automatically sit to your left and right.
Tip
b: Want one spicy half and one mild half? Add a copper or iron ingot to convert a nine-grid pot into a Yuanyang or four-grid pot; see Stoves & Hotpots.

blocks.t: Step 3: Add broth
Hold a filled bucket and right-click the pot to pour it in. Different containers make different broths:
Right-click the pot with　Resulting broth
Clear Broth: standard speed, suitable for any ingredient
Rich Stock: slowest (×0.85), milky white
Mushroom Broth: a little faster (×1.15)
Spicy Red Broth: fastest (×1.3), bright red
Once broth is added, a pot on the stove gives off steam. An empty pot will not light the stove.
Step 4: Add ingredients
With broth in the pot, hold a raw ingredient and right-click to add it. The pot has nine large cells in a 3×3 grid. Your crosshair determines which cell receives the food.

Start simply: vanilla raw beef, porkchops, mutton, and fish all work. For a more typical hotpot, try Raw Tripe (dropped by cows) or Fatty Beef Roll (cut with a kitchen knife). See Ingredients & Food Preparation.
Note
b: Put food in the pot. In 0.1.2-alpha, wood and iron items could also go in and get “cooked” into charcoal or iron nuggets. Avoid doing this (from 0.1.3-alpha-hotfix1 onward, pots only accept food).

blocks.t: Step 5: Craft chopsticks
Hold bamboo chopsticks and Shift + right-click the pot to open the hotpot screen: every ingredient in the pot is visible, and its appearance changes when cooked.
Step 6: Eat!
In the hotpot screen: with chopsticks on your cursor, left-click cooked food to eat it in one bite (complete with chewing sounds and a burp).

Pick up directly with chopsticks without opening the screen: hold bamboo chopsticks and right-click the pot directly to pick up a cooked portion from the targeted cell (it will notify you if there is no cooked food in that cell), then hold right-click to eat it.
Empty hands work too: right-click the pot with an empty hand (or holding a bowl) to scoop out cooked food directly from the targeted cell.
Watch out for cold pots: food will not cook without heat—eating from an unheated “cold pot” has a 30% chance of causing Nausea for 15 seconds.
After eating, don't forget: a heated pot keeps granting Regeneration I to players within six blocks, so invite your friends to share the meal.

◆ Short and tall stoves
Brick Stove: the short version. Its brick surface is level with a low hotpot table.

Tall Brick Stove: raises the firebox and pot by 10 pixels, to match a tall hotpot table. Its brick surface sits two pixels below the tabletop, while the pot rim extends three pixels above it for easy access.
A tall stove also occupies the block above it with an invisible block. Leave that space empty when placing one.
◆ Fuel and heat

Right-click the stove's brick body (or the stove itself when no pot is attached) to open the firebox screen and add fuel. Any vanilla furnace fuel works, with the same burn time as a furnace. There are three heat levels:
Fuel　Heat　Burn time (same as a furnace)
Wood items (planks, logs, sticks, wooden items, etc.)　×0.65　For example, planks: 15 seconds
Coal or charcoal　×1.0　80 seconds
Lava bucket　×1.6　1000 seconds
Tip
b: Fuel is consumed only while raw ingredients need cooking. If the pot has broth and the firebox has fuel but there is no raw food, the fire stays lit and the broth keeps boiling without consuming fuel. Take your time setting the table; you will not waste coal. A pot without broth will not light the stove.

blocks.t: The firebox screen has no temperature bar or remaining-time counter. The size of the flame shows how strongly it is burning.
◆ Types
Pot　Description
Iron Nine-Grid Hotpot / Copper Nine-Grid Hotpot　Nine-grid pot: one broth across nine large cells. Copper and iron differ only in appearance.
Yuanyang and four-grid pots　Available since 0.1.3-alpha-hotfix1; see Yuanyang and four-grid pots below.
Choose copper or iron, then select a pot shape below:
A pot is a separate block. It can sit on a stove, on the ground, or on a lit campfire (see below).
◆ Capacity

A nine-grid pot has nine large cells, each containing a 3×3 set of smaller slots: up to 81 portions per pot. Ingredients go into the large cell under your crosshair. If that cell is full, you cannot add more there.
◆ Broth bases
Add this　Broth　Cooking speed　Notes
Clear Broth　×1.00　Clear and light
Rich Stock　×0.85　Milky white; slowest
Mushroom Broth　×1.15　Pour in the stew; the bowl is returned
Spicy Red Broth　×1.30　Bright red; fastest
Tomato Broth　×1.10　Craft a broth bucket from hotpot base + water bucket, or add base to Clear Broth
Three Delicacies Broth　×1.00　Same method with Three Delicacies Hotpot Base

Hotpot bases: Tomato Hotpot Base uses tomatoes; Three Delicacies Hotpot Base uses fish, mushroom, carrot, and kelp (see the Recipe Collection). Add base to Clear Broth in the pot, or pour in a prepared broth bucket. Added in 0.1.4-alpha.
Add broth: hold the bucket or mushroom stew and right-click the pot. A regular pot holds only one broth at a time; divided pots are different.

Remove broth: right-click with an empty bucket to recover its original contents (water returns as a water bucket). Mushroom broth requires a bowl and no food remaining in the pot; take all food out first.
Serve soup to drink: right-click with a bowl. Cooked food is collected first; if there is none, you get soup. See Tableware & Drinks.
◆ Four heat levels for Spicy Red Broth
Spicy Red Broth can be "turned up" — not with chili powder, but by actually throwing chili peppers into the pot.
Level　Effect on food cooked in that pot
Mild (just poured)　Strength I for 6 s, Speed I for 6 s, no Hunger
Medium Spicy　Strength II for 9 s, Speed I for 9 s
Extra Spicy　Strength II for 12 s, Speed I for 10 s, Fire Resistance 15 s and Hunger I 6 s (spice opens the appetite and burns it off)

Level 3 Extreme Spicy　Strength II for 15 s, Speed I for 12 s, Fire Resistance 30 s, Hunger I 8 s; your mouth also catches fire for 2 s afterwards (you have Fire Resistance, so no damage; wearing a cloth apron prevents the flame)
How to adjust it:

Hold a Chili Pepper chili pepper and right-click the red broth area: the heat goes up one level, a burst of flame rises from the pot, and the action bar reports something like "Broth spiciness increased to: Extra Spicy". At Insane Spicy it only shows a hint and the pepper is not used up.
Ice to the rescue: plain Ice lowers the heat by 1 level, Packed Ice by 2, and Blue Ice drops it straight back to Mild. White steam and splashes rise from the pot.
Clicking a different broth with chili or ice shows "Only spicy red broth can be adjusted with chili or ice" and nothing is put into the pot.
Yuanyang and four-grid pots track each side separately: only the side you click changes. Pouring broth, scooping it, swapping broths or emptying the pot all reset the heat to Mild.

A bowl of Bowl of Spicy Red Broth scooped from the pot also keeps the heat level at the moment it was scooped and gives the matching effects when drunk. Cooked food from the pot shows a line like "Broth: Spicy Red Broth · Extra Spicy" in its tooltip.
Tip
b: Play the heat levels against chili oil, honey and vinegar: chili oil adds Fire Resistance, while honey and vinegar clear the Hunger that spicy broth brings. Food dipped in honey or vinegar will not leave you hungry from the heat, and your mouth will not catch fire. （Development Preview）You can also adjust spicy level duration steps, Fire Resistance, and mouth-fire thresholds under the "Spicy Broth Levels" group in Numeric Config.

blocks.t: ◆ What the broth adds to your food

Food cooked in a pot carries the flavour of that broth — hover over it and the tooltip adds a line like "Broth: Mushroom Broth" (spicy red broth also shows the heat level). Eating it grants an extra effect:
Broth　Extra effect from food cooked in it
Clear broth　Speed I for 15 s (clean and light on your feet) plus 1 tick of Saturation
Rich stock　Resistance I for 15 s plus Absorption I for 30 s (beef bones and old hen, sturdy and nourishing — no more Slowness)
Mushroom broth　Regeneration I for 10 s (mountain mushrooms, gets the blood moving)
Spicy red broth　Strength plus Speed by the heat level of that side; Extra Spicy and above add Fire Resistance and Hunger, see the table above
Tomato broth　Haste I for 15 s (sweet and tart, keeps you sharp), and clears Nausea
Three Delicacies Broth　Water Breathing for 20 s plus Luck I for 30 s (dried scallops and shrimp, fortune smiles)

It works the same whether you pick it up by hand, eat it with chopsticks, or put it in a bowl first. Simmer a batch in mushroom broth to keep healing, or cook a pot of Three Delicacies Broth and take it diving.

Hovering over a dish or soup bowl, the item tooltip indents and lists every status effect it grants and how long it lasts right below the broth name, one per line, such as "Strength II (0:15)" or "Speed I (0:12)" — blue for benefits, red for drawbacks (Hunger from spicy red broth). Food dipped in honey or vinegar no longer adds Hunger, so it is not listed either. A bowl of broth scooped from the pot lists its effects the same way.
◆ How food cooks
Raw ingredients turn into cooked food using their smoker / campfire recipes. Anything that can be cooked in a smoker can be cooked in the pot. Cooking time is:

b: Time per portion = smoker cooking time ÷ (fuel heat × broth multiplier)

blocks.t: For example, raw beef takes five seconds in a smoker. Coal + Clear Broth also takes five seconds; Spicy Red Broth (×1.3) takes about 3.8 seconds, while wood (×0.65) takes about 7.7 seconds. Small ingredients such as fatty beef rolls, potato slices, and meatballs take half as long as a whole cut of meat, making them quick to cook.
See the cooking section of the Recipe Collection for each ingredient's cooking times.
Note
b: Only put food in the pot. In 0.1.2-alpha, wood, ores, and iron items could also be added and “cooked” into charcoal or iron nuggets using furnace recipes. Avoid doing this. From 0.1.3-alpha-hotfix1 onward, pots only accept food: edible items or items with smoker / campfire recipes. Cooked food cannot be added again.

blocks.t: ◆ Ways to add and remove things
What you are holding　Right-clicking the pot does this
Raw ingredient　Adds it to the large cell under your crosshair
A plate of food　Tips raw ingredients into randomly chosen large cells with space; cooked food stays on the plate
Bamboo chopsticks holding raw ingredient　Places that food in the targeted large cell (into the pot)
Bamboo chopsticks holding cooked food　Eats it (works even when full; sneak + right-click a bowl or plate to put it back)
Bamboo chopsticks (empty)　Picks up a cooked portion from the targeted cell (notifies you if there is none); hold right-click to eat once picked up
Bamboo chopsticks + sneak (Shift)　Opens the hotpot screen
Bucket　Adds broth to an empty pot, or scoops broth with an empty bucket
Bowl　Collects cooked food or serves soup
Empty hand　Collects cooked food from the targeted cell
Empty hand + sneak (Shift)　Packs a stove-mounted pot, including broth and food, into your inventory (also works for standalone / campfire pots from 0.1.3-alpha-hotfix1)
Tip
b: Chopsticks and empty hands take the food currently visible at the surface; if it is still raw, you are told it is not cooked yet. A bowl first takes the visible cooked portion, then other cooked food, up to 3 portions.

blocks.t: ◆ Hoppers and pots
A hopper above the pot only inserts raw ingredients that can be cooked, one portion per slot; anything else stays in the hopper.
A hopper below the pot (or stove) only pulls out cooked food; raw food stays in the pot to keep cooking.
Hold bamboo chopsticks and Shift + right-click the pot to open it (right-clicking directly picks up a cooked portion without opening the screen). Inside the screen:
Every portion is visible, with different appearances for raw and cooked food.
With chopsticks on your cursor, left-click cooked food to eat it in one bite, restoring hunger and saturation just like vanilla food (works even when full).
Double-click to collect matching cooked food onto your cursor, like double-clicking in the vanilla inventory.
Hover over food to see its name. Dipped food also lists “Dipped: …”.
Holding dipping sauce in your main hand or off hand will automatically dip each bite eaten in this screen.
◆ Cold pots

A pot is cold when it is not on a burning stove or lit campfire. The broth is still and ingredients float in it. Eating from a cold pot with chopsticks has a 30% chance of causing Nausea for 15 seconds—avoid cold food to keep from upsetting your stomach (（Development Preview）chance and duration can be adjusted under the "Cold Pot Nausea" group in Numeric Config). Drinking a Plant Protein Drink, a bowl of clear broth, or dipping with vinegar clears it.
You can cook without a stove by placing the pot on a lit campfire or soul campfire:

In 0.1.2-alpha, the pot sits directly on the campfire. From 0.1.3-alpha-hotfix1, four slender iron supports rest on the campfire logs, so the pot no longer appears to float and flames no longer pass through it.
Heat equals coal, no fuel is consumed, and nearby players are healed too; the screen shows that the pot is heating.
Extinguishing or breaking the campfire makes the pot cold.
In 0.1.2-alpha, you had to mine this pot to pick it up. From 0.1.3-alpha-hotfix1, Shift + right-click with an empty hand packs it with broth and food, just like a stove-mounted pot.

A heated pot refreshes Regeneration I for 10 seconds every four seconds on players within six blocks, like a beacon's area effect. Staying beside a pot keeps restoring health, and sharing a table makes it even livelier. （Development Preview）(Interval, radius, duration, and level can be adjusted under the "Pot Warmth Healing" group in Numeric Config; set duration to 0 to disable.)

Craft a divided pot from a nine-grid pot and matching copper / iron ingots: ingot to the left = Taiji Yuanyang; below = Round-Center; above = straight divider; one on each side = four-grid pot; one above and one below = Square-Center Yuanyang. Each compartment holds its own broth. Aim at a compartment to add or remove its broth. Each food slot cooks with that compartment's broth; a compartment without broth will not cook. Like nine-grid pots, these work on the ground, campfires, short stoves, and tall stoves.
Pot　Divider　Broths　Capacity per compartment
Taiji Yuanyang　S-shaped, like a yin-yang symbol　2　28 on each side
Round-Center Yuanyang　A ring in the middle　2　44 outside, 9 inside
Straight-divider Yuanyang　One straight central divider　2　36 on each side
Four-grid hotpot　A cross dividing four compartments　4　16 per compartment
Square-Center Yuanyang　A square ring in the middle　2　44 outside, 9 inside
Note
b: In 0.1.4-alpha, S-shaped and O-shaped pots were renamed Taiji Yuanyang and Round-Center Yuanyang, including their item IDs. The four renamed pots already placed in worlds from 0.1.3 or earlier will disappear (two each in copper and iron).

blocks.t: Open the screen with bamboo chopsticks (Shift + right-click the pot). As with a nine-grid pot, small slots fill the pot from the edges inward. Spaces too close to a divider to fit a full slot are left empty, showing only broth and the pot bottom. Food floats at several positions in each compartment (S: four per side; O: six outside and two inside; straight: three per side; four-grid: two per compartment). Items sharing a position take turns bobbing to the surface.

In the screen, double-clicking matching cooked food or collecting it with a bowl only combines food from the same broth. Compartments with matching broths can be collected together; otherwise, only the selected side is collected.
Iron recipes are the same: replace copper ingots and the copper pot with iron equivalents.
Mine the pot: only the pot is removed. Broth and food are packed into its item and restored when placed again. In Creative mode, middle-click also copies the complete pot with broth and food.
Standalone pots stay in place even with air underneath.
Mine the stove's brick body: the whole stove is removed, and the packed pot drops too.
The pot item's tooltip lists its broth, food portions, and how many are cooked.
To remove a pot without mining the stove, Shift + right-click the pot with an empty hand.
Ingredients make the meal. This chapter explains where to find them, how to prepare them, and how much hunger they restore when cooked.
Tip
b: All raw ingredients can be cooked in the pot, or in a furnace, smoker, or campfire. The tables below list hunger restored per cooked portion. Cooked food cannot go back into the pot.

Source: cows and mooshrooms drop it using the same quantity rules as vanilla beef: 1–3 pieces, plus 0–1 per Looting level. Animals killed while burning drop cooked tripe.
Raw Tripe restores two hunger points; Cooked Tripe restores five.
Great for hotpot: about 2.5 seconds to cook in the pot (half the time of a whole piece of beef).

entries.title: Beef Loin and Beef Loin Slices

blocks.t: Beef Loin: cows / mooshrooms have a 25% chance to drop an extra piece (+10% per Looting level; burning animals drop Cooked Beef Loin). Eaten raw, it restores three hunger points; cooking it whole produces Cooked Beef Loin, restoring eight, just like vanilla steak.
Beef Loin Slices, the hotpot cut known as diaolong: cut a loin with a kitchen knife on a cutting board, or use a stonecutter, to get three slices. Each restores one hunger point raw or three cooked.
Loin slices cook fastest in the pot (twice as fast as fatty beef rolls), finishing in just a few seconds.
Cooked Beef Loin cannot be sliced.

entries.title: Cutting board, kitchen knife, and rolling pin

blocks.t: Craft these three tools before preparing ingredients:
◆ Cutting board
Tip
b: Directional placement, visibility while held, mining only the food on top, and brighter inventory icons are all improvements introduced in 0.1.3-alpha-hotfix1. In 0.1.2-alpha, the board has no facing direction, is barely visible in hand, and breaks together with the food on it.

blocks.t: Two logs of any type placed side by side horizontally yield two cutting boards (any wood type).
Directional placement: the board follows your placement direction and food faces you.
Hold something that can be cut or pounded and right-click the board to place one item. Right-click with an empty hand to take it back.
Mine the food on top to remove just that item in one hit, leaving the board.
◆ Iron Kitchen Knife
A square-tipped Chinese cleaver with 250 durability. It also works as a weapon, dealing four damage.
Tip
b: The orientation is baked into the texture: handle at the lower left, tip at the upper right, edge facing lower right. The inventory, the held item, the in-game Hotpot Guide, the web tutorial and the viewer all look exactly the same, because nothing flips the model any more — re-running the texture generator cannot flip it back either. When held in hand the blade ends up on the other side, matching the inventory icon; that is expected.

blocks.t: ◆ Rolling Pin
Has 120 durability and is used to pound meatballs.
Place an ingredient on the board, then right-click with the Iron Kitchen Knife to cut:
On the board　Cuts needed　Output　Hunger per cooked portion
Raw Beef Raw Beef　1　3 Fatty Beef Roll　3
Raw Mutton Raw Mutton　1　3 Mutton Roll　3
1　3 Beef Loin Slice　3
Potato Potato　3 cuts, 1 portion per cut　3 portions of Potato Slices (three slices in each portion)　2
Tofu (Cold) Tofu (Cold)　1　3 portions of Tofu Cube (Cold)　2
Tofu (Hot) Tofu (Hot)　1　3 portions of Tofu Cube (Hot) (already cooked)　2
Shortcut: use a stonecutter to prepare the whole batch at once.
Note
b: In 0.1.2-alpha, potatoes and tofu cannot be placed on the cutting board due to a known issue (use a stonecutter instead). This is fixed in 0.1.3-alpha-hotfix1.

blocks.t: Suitable ingredients: raw beef, porkchops, mutton, cod, and salmon.
Place the meat on the board.
Right-click the board with a Rolling Pin three times:
First hit: crush the meat.
Second hit: turn it into a paste.
Third hit: produce three raw meatballs.
The meatballs are small 3D spheres. Cook them in the pot; each cooked meatball restores three hunger points.
Ingredient　Raw meatball
Raw beef　Beef Meatball
Raw porkchop　Pork Meatball
Raw mutton　Mutton Meatball
Raw cod / salmon　Fish Ball
◆ Cilantro meatballs

Combine two raw meatballs with one Cilantro in a shapeless crafting recipe to get two cilantro meatballs. All four meatball types have cilantro variants. Each cooked one restores four hunger points, more than a plain meatball.

entries.title: Shrimp, peeled shrimp, and shrimp paste

blocks.t: Shrimp: caught while fishing, roughly one in six fish catches.
Peeled Shrimp: cut a shrimp with a knife on the board, or use a stonecutter.
Shrimp Paste: pound peeled shrimp on the board with a rolling pin 3 times.
All three can be cooked in a pot or roasted. Cooked portions restore 3 / 3 / 4 hunger points respectively. Cooked Shrimp and Cooked Peeled Shrimp also have a small flavor line in their tooltips.
Place a raw porkchop on the cutting board and cut it once with an iron kitchen knife to get 1 Minced Pork; a stonecutter also works. (Pounding pork meatballs with the rolling pin is unchanged.)
Craft Minced Pork + 1 vanilla wheat (shapeless) to get 3 Raw Ham Sausages.
Cook Raw Ham Sausages in a pot, furnace, smoker, or campfire to get Ham Sausages.
Place a Ham Sausage on the cutting board and cut it once with a knife for 3 Ham Sausage Slices; a stonecutter also works. Raw ham sausages cannot be cut on the board.
Slices can be heated once more (pot, furnace, smoker, or campfire) to become Cooked Ham Sausage Slices; these cannot go back into the pot.
Tip
b: Remember the order: Raw Porkchop → Minced Pork → Raw Ham Sausage → Ham Sausage → Ham Sausage Slice → Cooked Ham Sausage Slice. Minced Pork is a crafting ingredient and cannot be eaten directly.

blocks.t: Soybeans: breaking short or tall grass without shears has a 15% chance to drop one.
Tofu (Cold): shapelessly craft three soybeans and one water bucket into a block of cold tofu. The bucket is returned.
One knife cut turns cold tofu on a board into three Tofu Cubes (Cold), each restoring two hunger points when cooked.
Tip
b: Since 0.2.2-alpha, tofu comes hot or cold (in 0.2.1-alpha and earlier it was "Tofu", "Tofu Cubes" and "Cooked Tofu Cubes", and a whole block of tofu stayed the same item after cooking):
Tofu (Cold)、Tofu (Hot)、Tofu Cube (Hot)
• Simmer a whole Tofu (Cold) in the pot for 10 seconds and it becomes Tofu (Hot). It is cooked: pick it up with chopsticks or by hand, but it cannot go back into the pot.
• Leave the hot tofu in the pot and, 30 seconds after it went in, it breaks into Tofu Cubes (Hot), the same number of portions. Grab it early if you want the whole block.
• Hot tofu can also be cut on the board into three Tofu Cubes (Hot). Cold tofu cubes cook into hot tofu cubes in a furnace, smoker, campfire or the pot.

• Server owners can change both times in the config file: cooking.tofu_cook_ticks (cooking, default 200 ticks = 10 s) and cooking.tofu_overcook_ticks (breaking apart, counted from when it went in, default 600 ticks = 30 s). Run /orientshotpot reload to apply.

blocks.t: Freshly fried crispy pork is the first plate to be emptied at any hotpot table.

Combine minced pork + vanilla wheat + 1 egg (shapeless, anywhere in the crafting grid) to get 3 portions of Raw Crispy Pork, restoring 1 hunger point. Still raw batter and peppercorn — don't eat it yet.

Cook raw crispy pork in a furnace (10 s) / smoker (5 s) / campfire (30 s), or drop it straight into the pot, and you get Crispy Pork, restoring 4 hunger points. Golden and crackling, best eaten with your fingers.

Freshly fried crispy pork can go back into the pot for a second swim: with coal and clear broth it takes about 7.5 seconds to turn into Boiled Crispy Pork, restoring 6 hunger points. Crisp outside, tender inside, and full of broth.
Boiled crispy pork is the end of the chain — it cannot go back into the pot (you'll get a hint), so enjoy it while it is hot.
Tip
b: Remember the order: Raw Porkchop → Minced Pork → Raw Crispy Pork → Crispy Pork → Boiled Crispy Pork. Want both textures? Fry half to eat straight away and save half for the pot.

entries.title: Dried tofu, tofu skin, and sweet potato skin

blocks.t: Cold tofu and potato slices are good for more than the pot — press them and cut them and you get four hotpot favorites that hold broth beautifully:
Make this　How to lay it out　Yield　Raw　Cooked
2 cold tofu side by side in a row　3　2　4
2 cold tofu stacked in a column　3　2　4
2 potato slices side by side in a row　3　1　4
2 potato slices stacked in a column　3　1　4
Dried Tofu is pressed firm and gets more bean flavour the longer you chew; Tofu Skin is dry and softens in seconds, so every fold soaks up broth.
Wide Potato Noodles are slippery — hold them with chopsticks carefully or they slide back into the pot; Sweet Potato Skin carries a hint of sweetness.
All four can be simmered in the pot or baked in a furnace, smoker or campfire. In the pot they take about 5–7.5 seconds: tofu skin and sweet potato skin 5 s, dried tofu and wide potato noodles 7.5 s.
Tip
b: A row and a column are two different recipes: cold tofu in a row gives Dried Tofu, in a column gives Tofu Skin; potato slices in a row give Wide Potato Noodles, in a column give Sweet Potato Skin. Lay them the wrong way and you get something else.

blocks.t: Enoki Mushroom: craft 2 with 2 brown mushrooms, or break brown / red mushrooms themselves for a 50% chance to get a handful. They cook in 2.5 seconds; Cooked Enoki Mushroom restores 3 hunger points — thin strands that drink up the broth.

Bok Choy: breaking short or tall grass has a 15% chance to drop one bunch, no shears needed. Simmer a whole bunch for 2.5 seconds for Cooked Bok Choy, restoring 3 hunger points; the freshest bite in a table full of red broth.

Lotus Root: breaking lily pads has a 50% chance to drop a segment (shears will not get it). A whole segment cannot go into the pot — put it on the cutting board and cut 3 times, one slice per cut, or use a stonecutter to get 3 Lotus Root Slices at once. Slices cook in 5 seconds; Cooked Lotus Root Slices restore 3 hunger points, crisp and sweet, with broth hidden in every hole.

Raw Squid: squid and glow squid drop 1–2 (plus 0–1 per Looting level). A whole squid cannot go into the pot either — one knife cut (or a stonecutter) gives 3 Squid Rolls, already scored in a wheat-ear pattern; 5 seconds in the pot turns them into Cooked Squid Rolls, restoring 4 hunger points, curling up as they cook.
All of these can be baked too: furnace 10 s, smoker 5 s, campfire 30 s — baked and simmered taste the same.
Tip
b: Enoki mushrooms and bok choy are in the fastest tier (as quick as beef loin slices and tripe); lotus root slices and squid rolls are medium; dried tofu and wide potato noodles a little slower. Trying to put a whole lotus root or a whole raw squid in the pot tells you to cut it first.

blocks.t: Combine 1 vanilla wheat + 1 egg + 1 scallion + 1 bowl (shapeless, anywhere in the crafting grid) to get 1 bowl of Egg Fried Rice.
It restores 7 hunger points — golden egg around every grain, a scatter of green scallion, perfect for cooling down a spicy broth.
Egg fried rice is a finished dish: it does not go into the pot, and the bowl is part of the recipe, so the whole thing is eaten in one go.
Breaking short or tall grass has a 15% chance to drop a Chili Pepper, no shears needed.
It can be eaten directly (1 hunger point) for a clean hit of heat, or placed on the cutting board and cut once with a knife (or a stonecutter) for 2 portions of Chopped Millet Chili.
Chopped Millet Chili is the 14th seasoning at the sauce station: anything dipped in it gives Strength I for 8 seconds.

Most importantly, chili peppers turn up the heat of spicy red broth: hold a chili pepper and right-click the red broth area to raise the heat level, up to Extreme Spicy; ice brings it back down. See Stoves & Pots.
Note
b: Neither chili peppers nor chopped millet chili go into the pot: clicking the pot with them only changes the heat level or shows a hint, and they are never treated as an ingredient. For heat in your food, raise the level of the red broth.

blocks.t: Punching short grass / the lower half of tall grass (no shears) has a 15% chance to drop a Houttuynia Root (the root of fish mint) — the same odds as bok choy and peanuts.
You can eat it raw (restores 1 hunger point): crisp, pale white and jointed, with that fishy aroma people from the southwest know and love.
Put the whole root on the cutting board and hit it once with the kitchen knife (or use a stonecutter) to get 3 Houttuynia Root Slices. The whole root cannot go into the pot — slice it first.
Throw Houttuynia Root Slices into the hotpot for 10 seconds (200 ticks) to get Cooked Houttuynia Root Slices (restores 3 hunger points). A furnace, smoker or campfire also cooks them.
You can also pound the whole root on the cutting board with the rolling pin, 3 hits: hit 1 is still the root, from hit 2 on it turns into a little pile of mince, and hit 3 drops 2 Minced Houttuynia.
Minced Houttuynia is the 15th seasoning on the sauce station: dip a dish in it and you get Resistance I for 10 seconds plus poison cure — houttuynia is a cooling, detoxifying herb after all.
Tip
b: Most of the fishy smell cooks off: raw houttuynia is pungent; after a 10-second dip only a faint sweet aftertaste is left. If you are new to it, blanching it in the pot first is the safest way in.

blocks.t: Break short grass or the lower half of tall grass without shears. Scallions and cilantro each have a 25% drop chance.
Both can be eaten raw for one hunger point. They are also dipping sauce ingredients, and cilantro can make cilantro meatballs.
Grass also drops tomatoes for hotpot base, garlic for garlic paste, and soybeans for tofu.
Cooked Kelp: cook vanilla kelp in a hotpot to restore 2 hunger points. Furnaces, smokers, and campfires still produce dried kelp.

（Development Preview）Default drop chances for grass, lily pads, mushrooms, and beef loin can all be adjusted in Numeric Config or under "Loot Drops" in the settings screen (tomatoes now have their own separate entry; changes require /reload to take effect).

Tip
b: Not sure how long to simmer something? Four tiers cover it: beef loin slices, tripe, enoki mushrooms and bok choy cook fastest; fatty beef rolls, mutton rolls, potato slices, tofu cubes, ham sausage slices, peeled shrimp, lotus root slices, squid rolls, tofu skin and sweet potato skin are quick; dried tofu, wide potato noodles, meatballs and crispy pork are medium; whole beef loin and houttuynia root slices are slowest. See the "Cooking" table in Recipes for exact times — or tweak them in the config file.

blocks.t: A good dipping sauce completes a hotpot meal. The mod uses a self-service sauce station: nine small bowls let you mix your own sauce. Each seasoning has its own effect, and all effects stack.
In this chapter
Click an entry below to jump to it; you can also use the bookmarks along the top, or the triangle at the bottom right to turn page by page.
Sauce stations　Appearance: three ascending tiers,…
15 seasonings　Since 0.1.4-alpha, garlic drops fr…
Placing sesame paste and oyster sauce　Besides being used to mix sauces a…
Mixing a sauce　Hold a vanilla bowl (Bowl) and rig…
Dipping food　There are three ways:
Appearance: three ascending tiers, low at the front and high at the back, with three white porcelain bowls per tier: nine in total.
Height: 1.5 blocks tall, occupying two blocks, including an invisible block above. You can walk up the tiers.
Materials: 11 wood types plus iron, for 12 variants.
Facing: the front faces the player who placed it.
◆ Recipes
Each recipe makes one station. Replace planks with iron ingots for iron, or use the corresponding planks for other woods.
◆ Restocking the bowls
Right-click the station with an empty hand to open its restocking screen:
Nine slots correspond to the nine bowls on the station (there are 15 seasonings, with room for up to 9 kinds at once).
Each slot accepts one ingredient type. The ingredient placed in an empty slot determines its seasoning. Multiple slots can hold the same ingredient.
One ingredient = four servings of seasoning. A slot holds up to 16 ingredients, or 64 servings.
The ? in the top-right opens an ingredient reference, showing which ingredient makes which seasoning.
Stocked bowls visibly show their seasoning on the station.
Tip
b: Development preview: the ingredient list now uses a single paginated column. Clicking ? opens a narrow panel matching the main interface width, displaying names and effects in full with text wrapping; turn pages using the bottom arrows or the mouse wheel over the panel, and reopening it remembers your last page. The main interface and ingredient list are centered together, and installed JEI / REI will avoid this area.

blocks.t: Seasoning　Ingredient　Effect when eaten
MSG　Wheat　Restores two extra hunger points
Chili Oil　Blaze Powder　Fire Resistance for 10 seconds
Sweet and Sour Sauce　Sweet Berries　Speed for 10 seconds
Honey　Honey Bottle　Clears spice-induced Hunger and Poison
Sesame Oil　Sunflower or Pumpkin Seeds　Regeneration for five seconds
Vinegar　Apple or Beetroot　Clears Nausea and spice-induced Hunger
Sugar　Sugar　Haste for 10 seconds
Chopped Scallion　Scallion　Flavor only; no effect
Minced Cilantro　Cilantro　Flavor only; no effect
Garlic Paste　Garlic Paste　Resistance for 8 seconds
Oyster Sauce　Oyster Sauce　Water Breathing for 10 seconds
Sesame Paste　Sesame Paste　Absorption I for 10 seconds
Crushed Peanuts　Crushed Peanuts　Jump Boost I for 10 seconds
Chopped Millet Chili　Chopped Millet Chili　Strength I for 8 seconds
Minced Houttuynia　Minced Houttuynia　Resistance I for 10 seconds, cures poison
Since 0.1.4-alpha, garlic drops from grass. Pound it on a cutting board with a rolling pin 3 times to make 2 portions of garlic paste.
Each of the new ingredients has its own little story:

Oyster Sauce: shapelessly craft vanilla kelp + sugar + glass bottle for 2 bottles. The kelp you pick up by the sea finally has a purpose — dip in it and you can stay underwater without holding your breath.
Sesame Paste: peanut + wheat seeds + bowl makes 2 bowls. One rich spoonful takes the edge off the heat.

Crushed Peanuts: breaking grass has a 15% chance to drop a peanut. Put the peanut on the cutting board and pound it 3 times with a rolling pin for 2 portions of crushed peanuts (from the second hit the board already shows crumbs).
Chopped Millet Chili: one chili pepper cut once on the cutting board (or in a stonecutter) makes 2 portions. Chili peppers drop from grass. See Ingredients.

Minced Houttuynia: breaking grass has a 15% chance to drop a houttuynia root. Put the whole root on the cutting board and pound it 3 times with a rolling pin for 2 portions of mince. Houttuynia cools and detoxifies, so this dip cures poison and adds some resistance. See Ingredients.
“Cooling the spice” means clearing the Hunger effect from Spicy Red Broth. Every seasoning in your bowl contributes its effect when you eat dipped food.

entries.title: Placing sesame paste and oyster sauce

blocks.t: Besides being used to mix sauces at the station, sesame paste and oyster sauce can also be placed on the table as a decoration.

Place it: hold sesame paste or oyster sauce and Shift + right-click an empty spot on a hotpot table or tall hotpot table. Like chopsticks and sauce bowls it takes one plate slot, and several things can share that slot. It appears as a small 3D bottle matching its icon: sesame paste is a short labelled glass jar, oyster sauce a slim dark bottle.
Pick it back up: right-click it empty-handed to put it back in your inventory; mining the bottle takes only that bottle. Mining the table drops every piece of tableware in that slot.

Decoration only: a bottle on the table cannot be dipped into and cannot season food. To add this seasoning to a dish, go to the sauce station and mix a bowl as before (or dip at a sauce bowl on the table with chopsticks).
The bottle can still be eaten as before (same hunger value); placing it is just for looks.
Tip
b: Fill a slot if it fits: sesame paste, oyster sauce, sauce bowls and plates can share one slot — a row of bottles makes the table look like a real hotpot restaurant.

blocks.t: Hold a vanilla bowl (Bowl) and right-click a stocked seasoning bowl on the station. It takes one serving and becomes Dipping Sauce.
Want another seasoning? Hold that sauce bowl and right-click a different seasoning bowl to add it.
Rules:
Each seasoning can be added only once per bowl.
One sauce bowl lasts for nine dips.
After using some dips, you can still add seasonings you have not added yet. The remaining dip count stays the same.
An empty station bowl shows an “empty” message; restock it first.
The tooltip lists the seasonings and remaining dips.
Tip
b: Try sesame oil + vinegar + chopped scallions + chopped cilantro for Regeneration, relief from spice and Nausea, and a fresh onion flavor. Pair Spicy Red Broth with honey or vinegar to clear its spice effect.

blocks.t: There are three ways:
◆ ① Dip at the table
Place your sauce bowl on a table by right-clicking the tabletop, just like placing a plate.
Hold food with bamboo chopsticks and right-click the sauce bowl on the table to take a dip (clicking the sauce bowl with empty chopsticks will prompt you to pick up food first).
The food now carries the sauce's effects; hover over it to see “Dipped: …”. After taking the last dip, the sauce bowl turns back into an empty bowl.
◆ ② Automatic dipping at the pot

Hold dipping sauce in your main hand or off hand (either hand works); eating with chopsticks in the hotpot screen will automatically dip each bite, without taking it out first. Eating food held by chopsticks while aiming into the air (see “③” below) also automatically dips if you are holding sauce in hand.
◆ ③ Eat directly with chopsticks

Hold dipped food with chopsticks and hold right-click while aiming into the air to eat; the sauce's effects still apply. However you eat it—in the screen, with chopsticks, or from the table—dipped food keeps its effects.
Each dip uses one serving from the sauce bowl; after nine dips, the dipping sauce becomes an empty bowl.
Fill your hotpot table with plates of raw ingredients, bowls of soup, drinks to cool the spice, and chopsticks for picking up food.
In this chapter
Click an entry below to jump to it; you can also use the bookmarks along the top, or the triangle at the bottom right to turn page by page.
Plates　Five materials × six sizes = 30 pl…
Bowls and soup bowls　Vanilla bowls (Bowl) gain new uses…
Drinks　What's hotpot without something to…
Cloth apron　What people fear most at a hotpot …
Chopsticks　Chopsticks are the most commonly u…
◆ Types
Five materials × six sizes = 30 plates:
Material　Small dish ingredient
Quartz　Nether Quartz
Woven bamboo　Bamboo
Terracotta　Brick
Copper　Copper Ingot
Iron　Iron Ingot
Size　Shape　Food capacity
Small dish (1×1)　One slot　3 portions
Two-slot plate (1×2)　Two slots long　6 portions
Three-slot long plate (1×3)　Three slots long　9 portions
Four-slot square plate (2×2)　Square　12 portions
Five-slot long plate (1×5)　Five slots long　15 portions
Eight-slot platter (2×4)　Large　24 portions
Each slot holds up to three portions, including a small dish, so plate capacity = slots × 3.
◆ Crafting

Start with small dishes: place “material bowl material” in a horizontal row (with a vanilla bowl in the middle) to craft 2 small dishes. Combine matching small dishes to make larger plates. Quartz examples follow; use the corresponding dishes for other materials:
◆ Placement
Hold a plate and right-click a tabletop or the ground to place it.
Multiple plates fit in one block, without overlapping. Types can be mixed: up to five small dishes, two long plates, or one square plate per block.
Plates align automatically with the tabletop: five pixels lower on low tables, seven pixels higher on tall tables.
◆ Adding and removing food
These actions affect only the plate under your crosshair:
What you are holding　Right-clicking the plate does this
Plate　Places another plate
Food　Adds one portion (up to three per slot)
Bamboo chopsticks　Takes the last-added portion; right-clicking the plate again while chopsticks already hold cooked food = eats it (sneak + right-click to put it back)
Empty hand　Picks up the whole plate with its food
Empty hand + sneak　Takes the last-added portion into your inventory, leaving the plate
Mine a plate: only the targeted plate breaks, and its food drops too.
Middle-click: copies the targeted plate including its food.
Filled plates show their food in inventory icons and while held. Their tooltips work like vanilla bundles, combining matching items into “×quantity”.
Tip food into the pot: right-click the pot with a filled plate. Raw ingredients go in; cooked food stays on the plate.
◆ Vanilla bowls work too
Vanilla bowls (Bowl) gain new uses:
Place one on a table like a plate. It holds three portions and works as a small dish.
Right-click a pot with a bowl: it first collects cooked food (up to three portions). If there is none, it serves soup. Soup servings do not reduce the broth in the pot.
Right-click a pot with a bowl already holding food to tip the whole bowl into it.
◆ Six soup bowls
Served soup becomes a modded soup bowl item. All restore four hunger points, with different effects:
Soup bowl　Effect
Speed I for 15 s + Saturation for 1 tick; clears Nausea, including that caused by a cold pot (clean and light on your feet)
Resistance I for 15 s + Absorption I for 30 s (the Slowness debuff has been removed; high saturation, beef bones and old hen, sturdy and nourishing)
Regeneration I for 10 s (mountain mushrooms, gets the blood moving)

Strength + Speed (Mild: Strength I 6 s + Speed I 6 s; Medium Spicy: Strength II 9 s + Speed I 9 s; Extra Spicy: Strength II 12 s + Speed I 10 s + Fire Resistance 15 s + Hunger I 6 s; Level 3 Extreme Spicy: Strength II 15 s + Speed I 12 s + Fire Resistance 30 s + Hunger I 8 s). It carries the pot's heat level when scooped, see broth heat levels
Haste I for 15 s; clears Nausea (sweet and tart, keeps you sharp)
Water Breathing for 20 s + Luck I for 30 s (dried scallops and shrimp, fortune smiles)
Soup bowls return an empty vanilla bowl when consumed and can also be placed on tables.
Tip
b: To empty the pot and change its broth, scoop it out with an empty bucket, regardless of the broth type. Serving mushroom broth in a drinking bowl is a separate action.

blocks.t: What's hotpot without something to drink?
Drink　Effect per sip
Restores two hunger points; Speed for 15 seconds; cools the spice by clearing Hunger
Restores two hunger points; cools the spice and clears Nausea
Restores 2 hunger points; Speed and Haste for 15 seconds; the bottle bubbles
Each bottle has four sips. You can drink even with a full hunger bar. An empty bottle remains afterward and can also sit on the table.
Place drinks on a table and right-click to drink. Their tooltips show the remaining sips.
All three drinks have recipes: oranges for Orange Drink, soybeans for Plant Protein Drink, and cocoa beans and honey for Orient Cola. Oranges drop from oak and dark oak leaves.
◆ Glass cups

Right-click an empty cup with a drink bottle to fill it (Cup of Orange DrinkCup of Plant Protein DrinkCup of Orient Cola). One cup holds one sip; drinking leaves an empty cup. Cups can be placed on tables.
Finished bottles leave empty bottles (Empty Orange Drink BottleEmpty Plant Protein Drink Bottle), which can sit on tables or scoop drinks from cauldrons.

Cup of Water / Cup of Milk (Cup of WaterCup of Milk): right-click an empty cup with a water or milk bucket; the bucket stays full. An empty cup can also scoop from a water source. Water has no effect, milk clears all effects, and neither restores hunger.
◆ Toasting
Hold a filled cup with a drink in it (orange drink, plant protein drink, Orient Cola, water, and milk all count). There are three ways to toast:
Right-click a friend who is also holding a filled cup: both of you clink at once (their main or off hand must hold a filled cup too).
Nobody around? Hold Shift and right-click the air to raise your own cup (if a cup-holding player is within four blocks, you clink with them instead).
Right-click a filled cup placed on the table: tapping it against the table counts too.

The moment you toast: a crisp double chime (a light glass note plus a high ding), a little ring of splashes at the rim, and a few cheerful music notes. Both players get Luck I for 30 seconds + Regeneration I for 5 seconds, and the cup is marked — the next sip restores 1 extra hunger point (the tooltip reads "Toasted · Restores +1 bonus Hunger when drunk").

Drinking the cup turns it back into an empty cup and uses up the bonus, so toast again for more. Toasting unlocks the "Cheers!" advancement. （Development Preview）(Cooldown, Luck/Regeneration duration and level, and first-sip bonus hunger/saturation can be adjusted under the "Cheers Toast" group in Numeric Config.)
Tip
b: Best to start a hotpot meal with a round of toasts: Luck up, and your aim at the meatballs is steadier. Playing alone is fine too — Shift + right-click the air raises your cup just the same.

blocks.t: ◆ Drinks in cauldrons

Right-click a vanilla cauldron with a drink bottle or filled cup to pour it in. Each cauldron holds one drink type, up to 12 sips (3 full bottles); the surface rises once per 4 sips and takes the drink's color. Cola bubbles.

An empty cup scoops one sip. A vanilla glass bottle or an empty bottle of that drink scoops one bottle, up to 4 sips. Scooping the last sip leaves an empty cauldron. A different drink is rejected with a message.
What people fear most at a hotpot is hot oil and boiling broth splashing up — and a mouthful of insane heat setting your lips on fire. The cloth apron is made for exactly these two things.

Where it goes: the chestplate slot. On the inside it is invisible but it is real armor (3 armor points, 80 durability, the same tier as a vanilla leather chestplate); it wears down and can be enchanted normally.
Crafting: in the 3×3 grid, one piece of string on top makes the neck cord, and six white wool in the middle and bottom rows form the apron body.
Repairing: repair it on an anvil with white wool or string, matching the crafting materials.
◆ Three styles and recolouring
There are three styles of cloth apron. Their effect, durability, enchantability and repair materials are identical — only the fabric pattern differs:
Style　Look
Linen Cloth Apron Linen Cloth Apron　Plain linen, the default
Blue Print Cloth Apron Blue Print Cloth Apron　Indigo with tiny single-pixel white flowers
Brown Trim Cloth Apron Brown Trim Cloth Apron　Linen with dark brown trim all round and a small pocket on the hem
Recolouring: in a crafting grid, any style + a dye (shapeless) turns it into another style —
any style + white dye → linen
any style + blue dye → blue print
any style + brown dye → brown trim

Recolouring is the same apron with a new look: durability, enchantments and any custom name are all kept, and it only costs one dye. Adding the dye of the style it already is changes nothing (you get the apron back).
Tip
b: How it looks when worn: the apron sits close to the body and hangs from your chest down to just above the knees, one piece of cloth in front of both legs; when you walk, the hem swings forward with whichever leg steps out, and it lies flat on your lap when you sit. It only wraps a little around the sides; the sleeves and back are transparent, with just the neck strap showing behind your neck.

blocks.t: Once you wear it:

Level 3 Extreme Spicy does not faze you: eating a dish cooked in Level 3 (Extreme) spicy red broth, or drinking such a soup bowl, no longer sets those 2 seconds of flame on your lips (without the apron you still get them — they are pure spectacle and deal no damage).

Splashes bounce off: while you stand within 4 blocks of a lit stove, lit campfire, fire block or lava, fire, campfire, lava and hot floor damage no longer hurt you, and any flame that lands on you is snuffed out by the cloth. Walking through ordinary lava, being hit by mobs and falling still hurt as usual — this is a cloth apron; it stops splashes of hot oil and steam from close by, not an ocean of fire.
Tip
b: Too far from the pot and it does nothing: the splash protection only works when a heat source is within 4 blocks. Take the pot away or let the fire die, and the apron is just a piece of cloth clothing.

blocks.t: Chopsticks are the most commonly used tool in this mod:
Open the hotpot screen: hold bamboo chopsticks and Shift + right-click the pot.
Pick up cooked food from the pot: right-click the pot directly to pick up a cooked portion from the targeted cell (it will notify you if there is no cooked food in that cell).
Pick up food from bowls and plates: right-click a bowl or plate to pick up the last-added portion.
Add food to the pot: right-click the pot while holding a raw ingredient to place it in the pot.
Eat: while holding cooked food, hold right-click to eat it. You can eat even when full (the hunger bar stays put, saturation is still added). Any dipping-sauce effects apply too.
Put food back: sneak + right-click the center of a bowl or plate while holding food; the food goes back and the chopsticks stay in your hand.
Dip: right-click a sauce bowl on the table while holding food with chopsticks to take a dip; see Dipping Sauces.

Rest on bowl or plate rims (Development Preview): Shift + right-click the rim; chopsticks rest pointing toward the center from whichever side you click, and chopsticks holding food will rest along with the food. When clicking the center of a bowl or plate, empty chopsticks rest on the side closest to the player based on player facing (chopsticks holding food will still place the food or dip first). The resting angle snaps to steps of 22.5°; right-click with an empty hand to retrieve the chopsticks, and breaking the bowl or plate drops the chopsticks too.

Lay them straight on the tabletop: aim at an empty spot on a hotpot table or tall hotpot table and hold Shift + right-click; any held food is kept, and a white porcelain mini chopstick rest is added automatically. Development Preview: two straight bamboo sticks about 8.5 pixels long lie parallel with their tips resting across the white porcelain saddle and ends resting on the table; tips point where you face, ends point toward you, placeable in all four cardinal directions. They land on the nearest empty spot near the clicked position, occupying 9.5×4.5 pixels; a prompt appears if they don't fit without consuming items. Right-click with an empty hand or mine them to retrieve both the chopsticks and held food as they were, without dropping a separate chopstick rest.
Tip
b: Resting on a bowl or plate rim is one position; the mini rest on a tabletop is another. To move the chopsticks, right-click them with an empty hand first, then place them again.

blocks.t: Tip
b: Eat even when full: every food in this mod (raw and cooked ingredients, soup bowls, tripe, scallions, cilantro, drinks, and so on) can be eaten with a full hunger bar. The hunger bar does not rise, but saturation is still added, up to 20. Always Eat is compatible.

blocks.t: Hotpot is best shared around a table. There are two matching sets: a low set close to the ground, like a home hotpot table, and a tall set with 1.5-block-high tables, like a restaurant. Both come in 11 wood types:
Oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, bamboo, crimson, and warped. Tables use vanilla plank textures, and their recipes simply swap in the matching planks.

The tabletop is level with a short stove's brick surface, so a stove can fit seamlessly into a row of tables.
The underside resembles an upside-down stair, recessed four pixels on the outer side to leave knee room.
Automatic connections: any side next to another low or tall table, or a stove, fills in to create long tables.
Wooden tables are flammable and can be mined quickly with an axe.
1.5 blocks high, with an overhanging tabletop. The legs occupy pixels 0–19 and are recessed four pixels on the outside too.
The lower block is vanilla bricks, with wooden planks above it; this is why the recipe uses three brick blocks.
Pair them with a tall stove. When the stove opening faces a table, the table removes the bricks on that side and keeps the wooden part, leaving the firebox visible.
They also connect automatically to low tables and stoves.
Targeting accounts for their extra height, so plates and bowls on the tabletop can still be selected.
◆ Decorating the table
Plates, bowls, drinks, and sauce bowls sit on the tabletop; see Tableware & Drinks.
Small decorations such as lanterns, flower pots, candles, and cakes sit flush with the tabletop instead of floating.
Other regular blocks follow vanilla placement: they float five pixels above low tables or sink seven pixels into tall tables. You can still use them as decorations.

There are 9 additional tabletop materials: smooth stone; polished andesite, diorite, granite, deepslate, and blackstone; quartz; cut copper; and iron. Each has a low and tall table, for 18 tables. Their bases remain red brick, with the tabletop made from the chosen material.
Seating　Height　Recipe yield
Low; sitting height about 7/16 of a block　3
One block high, with its top level with the table; sitting position raised to 1.25 blocks　3
Both come in 11 wood types. Use the corresponding planks in the recipes.
◆ Placement
Facing: seating and seated players face the direction you were looking when placing it.

Connecting: adjacent seats in a straight line connect automatically when they are the same height, even with different woods. Middle legs disappear and end legs move inward. Perpendicular seats do not connect. Each connected run is limited to 3 blocks; a further seat starts a separate run. In 0.1.2-alpha, seats must face the same direction; placing from the opposite side leaves them offset. From 0.1.3-alpha-hotfix1, they connect along the same line regardless of which side you stand on.

Tall benches have angled A-frame legs, drawn by code because vanilla models cannot rotate at such small angles; their collision and selection width matches the seat top so walking alongside benches stays smooth.
◆ Stacking benches into a ladder
One bench is exactly one block high, so a stack of them makes a perfect ladder of steps.
Hold a bench (not sneaking) and right-click a placed bench: it walks up the stack and lands on the very top, using one bench each time.
Aiming at the top face and placing normally does the same thing.
Up to 16 levels; higher than that will not go.

Once a stack is two or more high, it works as a ladder: walk or jump against any side of it and you climb up and down just like a vanilla ladder. A single bench does not trigger this, so you will not accidentally climb while walking around the table.
The top level still seats you: right-click the top bench with an empty hand just like a normal one. Middle levels (with a bench above them) cannot be sat on.
If someone stacks a bench above you while you are sitting, you get up automatically to make room.
Breaking works as usual; anyone sitting there is dismounted.
Tip
b: Stacking is quick and so is taking it apart: a few benches are all you need to reach something high or build an "upper bunk" next to the hotpot table. Stacking a bench onto a bench, or climbing the stack, unlocks the "Skyward Climb" advancement.

blocks.t: ◆ Sitting down
Right-click seating with an empty hand, or while holding something that is not a block.
Click the middle of a block to sit in the middle; click the join between two blocks to sit between them.
Leave at least one full block between players so they do not overlap.
Press Shift (sneak) to get up behind the seat.
Tip
b: Match the heights for a comfortable meal: bench + tall table + tall stove, or stool + low table + short stove.
